source.title: A graph neural network for the era of large atomistic models
source.authors: Duoduo Zhang; An-Yang Peng; Chun Cai; Wen-Tao Li; Yuan-Chang Zhou; Jin-Zhe Zeng; Mingyu Guo; Cheng-Qian Zhang; Bowen Li; Hong Jiang; Tong Zhu; Wei-Le Jia; Linfeng Zhang; Han Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary information are present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling of an atomistic graph neural network using validation energy MAE, extending the scaling-law question to atomistic models rather than language models and cross-entropy loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own DPA3 scaling sweep and downstream-property correlations. Comparisons to scaling results from other work are citations, not extracted results. The paper's other architecture and benchmark comparisons are not included unless they bear on the reported scaling behavior.
record.test_reason: The paper runs its own IsoFLOP-style scaling sweep of an atomistic GNN (DPA3) on OMat24. It fits power laws of validation energy MAE against Nopt, Dopt and compute. It also reports how downstream phonon-property errors track energy error. This makes it a new-setting test of V5 and V6, not of the language-model versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present DPA3 as an architecture paper. They claim its generalization error follows scaling laws, fitting power laws in Nopt, Dopt and compute with exponents unlike LLMs. They link energy-error reductions to downstream phonon-property gains, and note weaker scaling on the data-limited water/ice case.
record.recipe_differences: Uses IsoFLOP-style compute profiles, but studies an atomistic GNN using validation energy MAE and configurations rather than language models using held-out cross-entropy and tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports a weaker size-scaling pattern on the water/ice test case trained with 0.1% of the data; it attributes this to limited test configuration diversity and possible overfitting by larger models.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing LiGS order from 2 to 3 lowers accuracy, especially for forces, at L3 and L6 (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In atomistic GNNs, higher-order geometric features beyond angles do not improve and can hurt accuracy.

record.code_released: https://github.com/deepmodeling/deepmd-kit (after version 3.1.0); evaluation scripts and processed data: https://zenodo.org/records/16794488
record.problems: The scaling results are reported qualitatively in the text and a figure, with no uncertainty estimates stated. The scaling sweep does not report a small-run extrapolation test or the compute-optimal parameter/data growth laws. The water/ice comparison uses only 0.1% of the data for training and is described by the authors as having limited test-set configuration diversity.
record.rows_left_out: Other model benchmark results, including general comparisons on downstream datasets, were left out where they did not directly measure the scaling relationship or the stated energy-error/downstream-property relationship.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss. Atomistic results cover only about one decade per axis, not several orders of magnitude.
No test of extrapolating small-run fits to much larger runs.
Nopt(C) is found per budget, but no allocation exponent for N or D versus C is reported.
No fixed-parameter depth or width comparison.
Image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes are not tested; only atomistic potential-energy models are.
Fitting choices are not varied. The authors only remark that exponents differ from LLM trends.

missing.what: Monotonic size scaling L3→L6→L12→L24 on SPICE-MACE-OFF: energy LWAMAE 0.73/0.43/0.36/0.22, force 14.08/10.69/8.74/5.78.
Layer-norm update stops error scaling at about 1.3M parameters; SiLU becomes unstable above 2M parameters; the Add update keeps the scaling rate.
Size trends on the zeolite and DPA2 test sets, and on TorsionNet (L3→L24 MAEB 0.26→0.09).

record.verdict_notes: Each scaling axis spans only about one decade, so the power-law form is weakly constrained. Combining the Fig. 4 fits implies Nopt ∝ C^0.35 and Dopt ∝ C^0.67, with data growing faster. The authors do not state this, so V3 is left untested. The water/ice rows come from a data-bottlenecked regime that V1's scope condition would exclude.

versions.untested_parts: Tests atomistic validation energy MAE, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
Does not report testing whether fits from small runs predict substantially larger runs.
Uses fixed compute budgets and finds the minimum validation MAE over parameter counts, but does not report how optimal parameter count and training-data size each grow with compute.
Architecture ablations and LiGS-order comparisons are reported, but not a test of how much depth, width, or other architecture details change loss at fixed parameter count.
Tests atomistic GNN scaling on OMat24 and reports a limited-data water/ice comparison; does not test image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws generally.
Reports correlations between energy MAE and four phonon-related property MAEs on MDR; does not test a broad set of downstream tasks or other forms of downstream performance.

Reports exponents different from language-model trends, but does not vary fitting choices or directly test whether compute-optimal allocations depend on setup or whether fitted curves bend away from a power law.

relationships.condition: DPA3 IsoFLOP sweep on OMat24, single epoch
relationships.reason: Validation energy MAE follows fitted power laws in Nopt (exp 0.4465), Dopt (0.2296) and compute (0.1545) (r1–r3), though each axis spans only about one decade.
relationships.display_finding: Validation energy MAE had fitted power-law exponents of 0.4465 for optimal model size, 0.2296 for optimal data size and 0.1545 for compute, each over about one decade.

source_check.condition: DPA3 IsoFLOP sweep on OMat24, single epoch
source_check.reason: Section 2.4 and Figure 4 support r1–r3: validation energy MAE follows fitted power laws along the compute-optimal frontier. The displayed ranges are narrow and do not establish orders-of-magnitude extrapolation.

relationships.condition: Water/ice benchmark trained on 133 structures (0.1% data)
relationships.reason: Going from L12 to L24, energy error is unchanged and force error rises from 25.2 to 26.8 (r6, r7), although L6 to L12 improves (r4, r5). This is a data-limited regime.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing from L12 to L24 left energy error unchanged and raised force error from 25.2 to 26.8, despite earlier L6-to-L12 gains.

source_check.condition: Water/ice benchmark trained on 133 structures (0.1% data)
source_check.reason: Table S-3 supports improvement from L6 to L12 (r4–r5), followed by unchanged energy error and worse force error at L24 (r6–r7). Section 2.3 attributes the weaker scaling to limited configuration diversity and possible overfitting.

relationships.condition: Architecture ablation on MPtrj (Fig. S-3): layer-norm update with SiLU
relationships.reason: From the text, not the rows: with LN updates, error scaling stops at about 1.3M parameters and deeper models get worse. SiLU without SiLUT fails above 2M parameters. Scaling depends on architecture choices.
relationships.display_finding: Layer-normalization updates stopped error scaling around 1.3M parameters and worsened deeper models, while SiLU without SiLUT failed above 2M parameters.
